newsitem.title: USA: House Democratic women delay farm spending bill.
newsitem.headline: House Democratic women delay farm spending bill.

text.p: A protest by House Democratic women has delayed action on the fiscal 1998 agriculture appropriations bill.

During floor debate Thursday, Rep. Nancy Pelosi, a California Democrat, and other female Democrats used a series of procedural votes to tie up action. Pelosi and the others complained that House Republican leaders have blocked them from offering the amendments they want on the House floor.
The Democratic women "are basically drawing the line," a spokesman for Pelosi said. "They're saying we're going to be heard. We represent the American people too."
After a final procedural vote, which was approved 344-73, the House suspended work on the agricultural appropriations bill.

Earlier motions offered by the Democratic women were defeated by Republicans on a party line vote. However, in the face of the women's determination, most Republicans relented and voted to suspend work on the bill.
It was unclear whether the House would return to the farm spending bill or any other legislation Thursday.

In a statement, the Democratic women said they were protesting the Republican leadership's "unfair" decision on what amendments could be offered on the Foreign Operations spending bill, which should go to the floor next week.

The Democratic women were most upset about an amendment that Republican leaders have allowed to be offered that would "reinstate the gag rule on international family planning and... defund the U.N. Fund for Population Activities."

Although the Republican leaders also allowed opponents of that measure to offer an alternative amendment, they "did not allow a bipartisan amendment which had a better chance of success," the Democratic women said.
"No Democratic Congresswomen were consulted on the fate of this program that dramatically improves the health and chances of survival of both mothers and their children," they said.
"No Congresswomen were allowed to offer an alternative that could have had a better chance of passage," they added.
